overview: A community includes only the living organisms interacting in an area; an ecosystem adds the non-living environment they interact with.
genZNote: Community: the cast of living characters. Ecosystem: the cast plus the entire set and props (the physical environment) they interact with.

aspects.label: Components Included
aspects.valueA: Only biotic (living) components — all species populations in an area.
aspects.valueB: Both biotic and abiotic components together, interacting as a functional unit.

aspects.label: Focus on Energy/Matter Flow?
aspects.valueA: Focuses mainly on species interactions and composition.
aspects.valueB: Explicitly includes energy flow and nutrient cycling between organisms and their environment.

aspects.label: Example
aspects.valueA: All organisms living in a pond.
aspects.valueB: The pond community plus its water, sunlight, temperature, and nutrient cycles, functioning together.

overlay.examHighYieldNote: An ecosystem is defined by the functional interaction between a community and its abiotic environment — this is the level at which energy flow and nutrient cycling are studied.
overlay.memoryTrick: Community = just the living things. Ecosystem = living things + their physical environment, working as a system.
overlay.commonMisconception: A 'community' does not include soil, water, or climate — those abiotic factors only enter the picture once you're talking about the ecosystem level.
